items.text: Bank of America Private Bank's 2026 Study reports that 65% of young investors (Gen Z and Millennials) still prefer to receive investment advice from a human advisor.
items.quote: sixty five percent 65% still prefer to receive investment advice from a human advisor.
items.unit: share of young investors preferring investment advice from a human advisor

items.text: Bank of America Private Bank's 2026 Study reports that 47% of young investors use AI to research companies or markets.
items.quote: forty seven percent 47% of young investors use AI to research companies or markets
items.unit: share of young investors using AI to research companies or markets

items.text: Bank of America Private Bank's 2026 Study reports that 87% of young investors are comfortable with advisors using AI to help manage portfolios.
items.quote: eighty seven percent 87% are comfortable with advisors using AI to help manage portfolios
items.unit: share of young investors comfortable with advisors using AI to manage portfolios

cells.differs_because: These passages state how younger adults (roughly ages 25-45, not strictly under 40) trust financial information sources and their preference for human versus AI investment advice, not how clients under 40 choose (select) a financial advisor, and they are single-period snapshots rather than a series showing change over recent periods.
cells.reason: No passage states how clients under 40 choose a financial advisor or how that changed over time; the closest evidence is related but different: younger adults' trust in financial information sources and preference for human vs AI advice.
